data.subject: AI Basics - What is Artificial Intelligence?
data.desc: Artificial intelligence is no longer science fiction — it's a technology you use every day. But do you really know what AI is? This course, consisting of five short lessons, will take you on a journey from basic definitions to practical applications in your life. Most importantly, you'll understand the difference between what AI can really do today and what movies promise.

lesson.subject: AI Basics - What is Artificial Intelligence?
lesson.desc:
The first lesson is like a warm welcome to the wonderful world of artificial intelligence, starting from the very beginning. You'll discover a straightforward and easy-to-understand explanation of AI. You'll learn why it's not just a fictional concept but a real technology that's a part of your everyday life. I'm so excited to start this lesson with you! It's the foundation for all the others to come, and I'm here to make sure it's a gentle and accessible journey for all of us. No stress, no complicated terms — just a space where we can all grow together in comfort and ease.

What you'll learn

lesson.subject: The History of AI: From Turing to Today
lesson.desc: Let's dive into the captivating history of artificial intelligence — from the visionary ideas of Alan Turing in the 1950s to the amazing ways we use it today. You'll learn about the key moments in the development of AI and how our approach to defining machine intelligence has changed over time. This lesson shows that AI isn't just one idea, but a beautiful evolution of our thinking about technology.

lesson.subject: Contemporary Understanding of AI
lesson.desc: We're going to show you how we understand artificial intelligence today and why the modern approach is more practical than ever. You'll be amazed to discover that AI doesn't have to copy the human brain to be really helpful. Let me give you a specific example using Netflix. I'll break down how modern AI systems work in three simple steps that you'll easily understand and remember.

lesson.subject: AI categories – Narrow, general, and machine learning
lesson.desc: I'm so excited to share with you the most important lesson for understanding the current state of AI. You'll discover the fascinating difference between what we have today (narrow AI) and what researchers dream of (general AI). You'll learn what machine learning is and why it's such a game-changer in technology development. This lesson is designed to help you understand the strengths and weaknesses of today's AI in a realistic way.

lesson.subject: AI in Everyday Life: Practical Applications
lesson.desc: Get ready, because you're about to be pleasantly surprised! This lesson is going to be so interesting! We're going to take a look at how often you use AI without even realizing it. From morning to evening, you're surrounded by artificial intelligence. It's in your phone, your computer, your car, and even your home. You'll see some concrete examples, and you'll understand that AI isn't just some future thing — it's something you can experience right now. This is a practical summary of everything you've learned.

lesson.subject: Summary - What to remember about AI?
lesson.desc: A brief but key summary of the entire course. The five most important things about AI that you need to remember, presented in a way that will help you understand artificial intelligence on a daily basis. This is your AI download - everything you really need in one place. Plus tips on how to further develop your knowledge.

data.subject: Roles and Responsibilities
data.desc: AI Engineers are responsible for designing, developing, and deploying AI systems that solve real-world problems. Their roles include building machine learning models, implementing data processing pipelines, and integrating AI solutions into existing software or platforms. They work on tasks like data collection, cleaning, and labeling, as well as model training, testing, and optimization to ensure high performance and accuracy. AI Engineers also focus on scaling models for production use, monitoring their performance, and troubleshooting issues. Additionally, they collaborate with data scientists, software developers, and other stakeholders to align AI projects with business goals, ensuring that solutions are reliable, efficient, and ethically sound.
